text:
ana: Heads up — since the midnight maintenance we've seen a spike of GPU pod evictions in us-west1-b (mostly tiny training jobs). ~40 evicts in the last 10m. Any ideas?

mike: saw it too. warm-pool nodes not getting refilled, pods pending with `nodeSelector` + `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` affinity.

ana: repro stack from one pod: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x5 over 3m)  default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient gpu, 2 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 4 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector.
```

jordan: hmm — the maintenance removed a couple of rack-level BGP routes briefly, I think kubelet went NotReady on two nodes and our placement pinned many pods to remaining nodes because of AZ preference.

lee: can you paste the pod spec? wondering if affinity uses `topology.kubernetes.io/zone: us-west1-b` hard constraint.

ana: snippet: 
```yaml
nodeSelector:
  accelerator: nvidia-a100
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        podAffinityTerm:
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
```

mike: so with two nodes flapping in the same AZ we lost 30% of slot capacity and scheduler started preempting smaller pods to make room for big gangs. Warm-pool reclaiming is linear-slow because we hit API-server qps throttling during the incident.

jordan: ops-bot telemetry: `gpu_alloc_failures` spiked 5x at 2023-10-05T00:12:30Z, `node_ready_count` dropped from 24->22 for about 90s.

lee: quick mitigation: relax the preferred anti-affinity weight to 30 and relax nodeSelector -> allow fallback to `accelerator: any-gpu` for <8h. I can open a tiny rollout.

ana: agreed — please annotate so we can revert. Jordan can we hold patch that reintroduced aggressive rack-weighting? feels correlated.

jordan: pausing that rollout now (PR #4281). Also adding a guard in the scheduler: if nodeReady drop >2 in AZ within 2m, temporarily disable zone-weighting for 5m. Testing the rule locally.

mike: if we do that we should also log the event to the infra incident stream and emit a metric `scheduler_zone_lockouts` so SRE can alert.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2023-4389 — title: us-west1-b transient node flaps -> evict cascade. Pager policy: SRE on-call.

lee: rollout done for relaxed affinity (canary to 10% of schedulers). watching pod pending count.

ana: after the canary pending pending pods dropped from 72 -> 9 over 4m. looks promising.

mike: follow-ups: 1) revert aggressive rack weighting PR until canary proves safe; 2) add API-server burstQPS increase for warm-pool controller; 3) add compensating scheduling fallback for nodeSelector mismatch. I'll create tickets.

jordan: I'll keep the temporary scheduler guard and instrument it. logging rule: `scheduler.guard.zone_drop` with az, drop_count, timestamp.

ana: thanks all. assigning ops followups to jordan/mike/lee. ping me if it resurfaces. :thumbsup:
